[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The claim that session-length patterns differ across regions relies on regional session-length findings absent from this item’s LATAM-growth evidence binding.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The bound LATAM-growth fact supports only the LATAM install and session growth figures. The global and regional session-length claims are not supported by this item’s evidence binding.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The recommendation relies on distinguishing outcomes from a 2030 projection, an empirical premise not supported by the item’s downloads-only evidence binding.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] This states that the report pairs activity and spending with a longer-term projection, but the only bound fact concerns app downloads and supports neither spending nor the projection.

[public_editorial_quality.semantic_review] The bound fact supports the 2025 download figure only. The added consumer-spending increase and 2030 global-GDP projection are material assertions not supported by this item’s evidence binding.

[public_editorial_quality.material_limitation_omitted] The report represents the benchmark findings without disclosing a material source limitation: the canonical facts state that sample sizes are not stated and that underlying denominators are not stated for key install/session comparisons. This omission may affect how readers interpret the benchmark figures. The limitation is report-wide rather than localizable to one existing repair target. Dimensions: limitations: The public wording omits the source’s stated absence of sample sizes and, for key install/session comparisons, underlying denominators. That methodological uncertainty is material to interpreting the benchmark, but no existing item is a localized repair target for the report-wide caveat.
